colleges.name: Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay (IIT Bombay)
colleges.fees: Tuition fee is around ₹2.2 - 2.5 Lakhs per year. Total 4-year B.Tech cost including hostel, mess, and campus amenities is around ₹10-12 Lakhs.
colleges.placements: Average package overall is ₹21.8 LPA. Computer Science (CSE) average is around ₹28 LPA. Design (B.Des) average package is around ₹16 LPA.
colleges.admission: B.Tech requires JEE Advanced rank. B.Des requires UCEED rank.
colleges.caution: Extreme academic competition. Relative grading means you are constantly compared to peers. The workload is heavy and pressure can build up.
colleges.reddit_verdict: Unmatched brand status, startup network, and cultural life in India, but requires high mental resilience.

colleges.name: Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi (IIT Delhi)
colleges.fees: Tuition is ₹2.2 Lakhs per year. Total 4-year B.Tech cost including accommodation is around ₹10-11 Lakhs.
colleges.placements: Average B.Tech package is ₹20-22 LPA. Heavy placement presence from global giants like Google, Microsoft, McKinsey, and top hedge funds.
colleges.admission: B.Tech requires a top rank in JEE Advanced. B.Des requires a top rank in UCEED.
colleges.caution: Highly crowded, intense peer pressure, and Delhi's winter air pollution can be a challenge.
colleges.reddit_verdict: Excellent tech ecosystem, strong entrepreneurial support, and prime location for networking.

colleges.name: National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad (NID Ahmedabad)
colleges.fees: Approx. ₹3.8 Lakhs per year. Total 4-year B.Des cost around ₹15-16 Lakhs.
colleges.placements: Average package ranges from ₹8-12 LPA. Top interaction design/UX packages can go up to ₹20-25 LPA.
colleges.admission: NID Design Aptitude Test (DAT) - Prelims and Mains (Studio Test).
colleges.caution: Extremely selective (only ~100-125 general seats in B.Des nationwide). It is a pure design school, not a tech school; there is no coding or CS in the syllabus.
colleges.reddit_verdict: The gold standard for design in India. If you want pure product design or animation, NID has no equal.

colleges.name: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani (Pilani, Goa, and Hyderabad Campuses)
colleges.fees: Fees are high, approx. ₹5.5 - 6 Lakhs per year. Total 4-year B.Tech cost is around ₹24-26 Lakhs.
colleges.placements: Average package is ₹18-20 LPA overall across campuses. CS branch average is ₹25-27 LPA. Strongest startup culture in India alongside IITs.
colleges.admission: Requires a high score in BITSAT exam.
colleges.caution: No reservation quota (100% merit-based), resulting in very high academic cutoff peers. The fast-paced semester fee hikes are a common student grievance.
colleges.reddit_verdict: Excellent private alternative to IITs. The zero-attendance policy allows students freedom to build startups and side-projects.

colleges.name: Symbiosis Institute of Design, Pune (SID Pune)
colleges.fees: Approx. ₹4.2 Lakhs per year (tuition) + hostel/mess of ₹1.5-2 Lakhs per year. Total 4-year B.Des cost around ₹23-25 Lakhs.
colleges.placements: Average package is ₹6-8 LPA. Top placements reach ₹14-16 LPA, mostly in UX/UI design, graphic design, and user research.
colleges.admission: Symbiosis Entrance Exam for Design (SEED) + Portfolio Review and Personal Interview.
colleges.caution: Very high fees for a private design institute. Placement outcomes depend heavily on the strength of your personal design portfolio rather than the college brand name alone.
colleges.reddit_verdict: Great campus infrastructure and curriculum for UX/UI design if budget is not an obstacle.

colleges.name: Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT)
colleges.fees: Structured in 5 categories based on exam rank. Category 1 is ₹2 Lakhs/year; Category 5 is ₹5 Lakhs/year. Hostel is ₹1-1.5 Lakhs/year.
colleges.placements: Average package is ₹8-9 LPA. Computer Science (CSE) average is around ₹10-12 LPA. Recruiting is massive with 800+ companies visiting.
colleges.caution: Massive student intake (thousands in CS alone) leads to extreme competition during placements. Campus rules are famously strict (strict curfews, biometrics, rules for interaction).
colleges.reddit_verdict: A reliable backup option with decent placement statistics, but feels like an extension of school rules with strict supervision.

colleges.name: Manipal Institute of Technology (MIT Manipal)
colleges.fees: Approx. ₹4.5 - 5 Lakhs per year. Total 4-year B.Tech cost is around ₹20-22 Lakhs including hostel.
colleges.placements: Average package is ₹10-12 LPA. CSE and IT branch averages are around ₹14-16 LPA.
colleges.caution: High cost of living and expensive tuition. The student lifestyle and social options in Manipal require self-discipline to avoid distractions from studies.
colleges.reddit_verdict: Phenomenal campus life, liberal culture, and strong tech/coding clubs. Great placement opportunities for CS/IT branches.

colleges.name: Shiv Nadar University, Delhi NCR
colleges.fees: Approx. ₹4.5 Lakhs per year. Total 4-year B.Tech cost is ₹18-20 Lakhs.
colleges.placements: Average package is ₹10-12 LPA. CS branch average is around ₹15 LPA.
colleges.admission: SNUSAT entrance exam and subsequent personal interview.
colleges.caution: Located in Dadri/Greater Noida, which is relatively isolated from central Delhi. Strict academic rigor and grade standards.
colleges.reddit_verdict: A hidden gem. Great research funding, top-tier lab facilities, and highly flexible multidisciplinary majors/minors (like B.Tech with Design minor).

colleges.name: Ashoka University, Sonipat
colleges.fees: Approx. ₹10 Lakhs per year including residence. Note: Generous need-based financial aid is provided to over 45% of students.
colleges.placements: Average package is ₹10-12 LPA. Recruiting is strong from global consulting firms (McKinsey, Bain, BCG), analytics companies, and tech startups.
colleges.admission: Ashoka Aptitude Test (AAT), essays, and personal interview.
colleges.caution: Not a traditional engineering or vocational college. The focus is on Liberal Arts, critical thinking, and multidisciplinary education.
colleges.reddit_verdict: Top-tier humanities and liberal arts network in India, offering Ivy-League style academic rigor and networking.

colleges.name: Plaksha University, Mohali
colleges.fees: Approx. ₹8-9 Lakhs per year. Scholarships are available based on merit and financial need.
colleges.placements: Recent graduating batches have average packages around ₹12-14 LPA. Strong recruiting ties with modern tech firms and startups.
colleges.admission: Comprehensive application review, writing test, and personal interview.
colleges.caution: Very new university (founded in 2021). The brand name is still establishing itself among traditional public sector and conservative corporate employers.
colleges.reddit_verdict: Highly modern, interdisciplinary engineering curriculum (major focus on AI, Data Science, and Robotics) backed by top Indian business leaders.

colleges.name: Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Mumbai (TISS)
colleges.fees: Extremely low fees, approx. ₹60,000 - 1 Lakh per year including hostel accommodations.
colleges.placements: Famous for its MA in Human Resource Management (equivalent to MBA) with average packages around ₹25-27 LPA. Undergraduate programs average ₹6-8 LPA.
colleges.admission: CUET scores or specific university test.
colleges.caution: Historically politically active campus with a strong focus on social sciences and activism. Extremely few undergraduate seats.
colleges.reddit_verdict: Incredible value for money. The absolute best college in India for Human Resources and Development Studies.

colleges.name: National Institute of Fashion Technology, Delhi (NIFT Delhi)
colleges.fees: Approx. ₹2.8 - 3 Lakhs per year. Total 4-year B.Des cost is around ₹12-13 Lakhs.
colleges.placements: Average package is ₹5-8 LPA. Top fashion brands, retail companies, and design houses recruit here.
colleges.admission: NIFT Entrance Exam (consisting of General Ability Test, Creative Ability Test, and Situation Test).
colleges.caution: Workloads are intense with daily hands-on submissions, model building, and fashion show deadlines. Starting packages in fashion retail can be low compared to tech fields.
colleges.reddit_verdict: The premier fashion and communication design institute in India, but requires a strong portfolio and patience to grow your salary.

exams.name: Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) Main
exams.eligibility: Class 12 pass with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics (PCM). Max 3 attempts in consecutive years.
exams.structure: 3-hour computer-based test containing MCQs and Numerical Value questions in Physics, Chemistry, and Math (300 marks total).
exams.difficulty: Extremely high competition due to sheer numbers. Over 14 Lakh students appear for ~55,000 seats across NITs, IIITs, and government colleges.
exams.colleges_accepting: All National Institutes of Technology (NITs), Indian Institutes of Information Technology (IIITs), and state government engineering colleges.

exams.name: Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) Advanced
exams.eligibility: Must be in the top 2.5 Lakh rank holders of JEE Main. Max 2 attempts in consecutive years.
exams.structure: Two mandatory papers of 3 hours each on the same day. Highly unpredictable pattern, multiple-correct questions, list-matches, and negative marking.
exams.difficulty: One of the toughest exams globally. Requires deep conceptual logic, analytical deduction, and strong advanced calculus. Only ~17,000 total seats in IITs.
exams.colleges_accepting: All 23 Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) and Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology (RGIPT).

exams.name: Undergraduate Common Entrance Examination for Design (UCEED)
exams.eligibility: Class 12 pass in any stream (Science, Commerce, or Arts). Max 2 attempts in consecutive years.
exams.structure: Part A (2 hours, Computer-based): Visualization, spatial ability, observation, design concepts. Part B (1 hour, Paper-based): Drawing and design sketching.
exams.difficulty: Low conceptual math/physics load, but highly competitive. Only ~150-180 general seats are available in the top IIT B.Des programs, making the drawing evaluation cutoff very selective.
exams.colleges_accepting: IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Guwahati, IIT Hyderabad, IIITDM Jabalpur, and several private design colleges (as partners).

exams.name: National Institute of Design - Design Aptitude Test (NID DAT)
exams.eligibility: Class 12 pass in any stream (Science, Commerce, Arts).
exams.structure: Stage 1 (Prelims): Written exam on design theory, visual spatial logic, and sketching. Stage 2 (Mains): Studio test involving 3D model making, material handling, audio-visual tests, and interview.
exams.difficulty: Very high. Rote learning won't work here. The exam tests creative problem solving, hand-eye coordination, and spatial logic.
exams.colleges_accepting: All NID campuses (Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Kurukshetra, Vijayawada, Bhopal, Jorhat).

exams.name: Common Law Admission Test (CLAT)
exams.eligibility: Class 12 pass with minimum 45% marks (40% for SC/ST). No upper age limit.
exams.structure: 2-hour offline test containing 120 multiple-choice questions focusing on Reading Comprehension, Current Affairs, Legal Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, and Quantitative Techniques.
exams.difficulty: Moderately high. It is a speed-reading and comprehension test. Success depends heavily on vocabulary, scanning ability, and legal logic under time constraints.

exams.name: Common University Entrance Test (CUET) UG
exams.structure: Section 1: Languages, Section 2: Domain-specific subjects (PCM/Arts/Commerce), Section 3: General Test (General Knowledge, Aptitude). Computer-based test.
exams.difficulty: Moderate. Tests based directly on NCERT Class 12 syllabus, but high percentiles are required due to massive application numbers for top central universities.
exams.colleges_accepting: Central Universities (like Delhi University, BHU, JNU) and several state/private universities.
